top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct architecture from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion work: it cancels the trap light shift while keeping Lamb-Dicke confinement and many-atom averaging. It is mature, replicated across laboratories and species at the 10^-18 level, and Katori (concept and first strontium lattice clock) and Ye (accuracy frontier) have separable roles, so a two-name credit with a citation anchored on the lattice and its realisation is defensible. An award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No documented tie to Katori or Ye. My WACQT and Chalmers superconducting-circuit connections (Delsing, Wilson, Kockum) would matter only for circuit QED, which is not in this slate.
